constraints: Azure Functions supports only version 4.x of the runtime host; a function app pinned to an earlier major version keeps running but is not eligible for new features, security patches, or service support.
Raising FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION alone is not enough: the app settings, bindings, and function code can need changes, so follow the published migration guide for the version being left.
The runtime version is an app setting in Azure, and this rule fires only when the export writes the version into siteConfig.

steps.instructions: Follow the Azure Functions migration guide for the version being left, then set FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION to ~4 in the app's configuration.
steps.title: Migrate the function app to the v4 runtime

steps.instructions: Set the same version in the deployment source - the siteConfig.FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION app setting in an Azure Resource Manager or Bicep template, the version in host.json or the .csproj AzureFunctionsVersion for a function project, and the azurerm_function_app version in Terraform.
steps.title: Align the runtime declaration

verification.purpose: Confirm the app targets the v4 runtime.
Confirm the app is still reachable and deploying after the migration.

rules.summary: Azure Functions supports only version 4.x of the runtime host and ended support for version 1.x on 2026-09-14. A FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION of ~1 no longer receives security patches and the app is not eligible for Azure support.
rules.title: Azure Functions runtime 1.x is end-of-life

rules.summary: Azure Functions lists runtime versions 2.x and 3.x as retired, both at end of extended support since 2022-12-13. Apps on ~2 or ~3 are not eligible for new features, security patches, or service support, and v3 apps in the Linux Consumption plan stop running after 2026-09-30.
rules.title: Azure Functions runtime 2.x and 3.x are out of support
